chunks: Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Hammad, from al-Ruba'i, from al-Fudayl, who said:
I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: Among the matters are matters which are deferred with Allah; He brings forward from them what He wills and puts back from them what He wills.

key_terms.أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ: Abu Ja'far (Imam al-Baqir), a key narrator of this hadith

ai.seo_question: What does the concept of Bada' mean in Shia theology regarding divine decree?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates the doctrine of Bada', clarifying that it is not a change in Allah's eternal knowledge but rather the manifestation of specific divine decrees in accordance with His wisdom. It highlights that certain affairs are 'suspended' (mu'allaqah) with Allah, who actively chooses to accelerate or delay their occurrence based on His will, a concept central to Shia theology regarding divine providence and the interplay between fate and free will.

en.ammaar-muslim: 11. [11/369] al-Kafi: Muhammad b. Ismail from al-Fadhl b. Shadhan from Hammad from Rib’i from al-Fudhayl who said:
I heard Aba Ja’far عليه السلام saying: From the matters are matters which are deferred with Allah. He brings forward from them what He wills and puts back from them what He wills.
